chains.summary: Narada knows every science and says that he knows the words, not the self, and he grieves. Sanatkumara leads him inward. One speaks truth when one understands. One understands when one reflects. One reflects when one has trust. One has trust when one is steadfast. One is steadfast when one acts. One acts when one finds joy. Joy is in the vast, not in the small.
chains.title: Narada: learned and still grieving

verses.m: 'Sir, I know only the texts; I do not know the self. I have heard from people like you that one who knows the self crosses beyond sorrow. I am in sorrow, sir. Please take me across.' He said to him: 'Whatever you have studied is only name.'
verses.sa: सोऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविदेवास्मि नात्मविच्छ्रुतꣳ ह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्यस्तरति शोकमात्मविदिति सोऽहं भगवः शोचामि तं मा भगवाञ्छोकस्य पारं तारयत्विति तꣳ होवाच यद्वै किंचैतदध्यगीष्ठा नामैवैतत् ॥

verses.m: When one acts, one becomes steadfast. One does not become steadfast without acting; only by acting does one become steadfast. So action itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand action.'
verses.sa: यदा वै करोत्यथ निस्तिष्ठति नाकृत्वा निस्तिष्ठति कृत्वैव निस्तिष्ठति कृतिस्त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्येति कृतिं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥

verses.m: When one finds happiness, one acts. No one acts without finding happiness; only by finding happiness does one act. So happiness itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand happiness.'
verses.sa: यदा वै सुखं लभतेऽथ करोति नासुखं लब्ध्वा करोति सुखमेव लब्ध्वा करोति सुखं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यमिति सुखं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥

chains.summary: The joy one grows into by practice, like poison first and nectar in the end, is born of a clear understanding of the self. Pleasure from the senses is nectar first and poison after. The pleasure of sleep, laziness and heedlessness deludes from start to finish.
chains.title: Poison first, nectar after

verses.m: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, best of the Bharatas: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, and in which one reaches the end of sorrow.
verses.sa: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥

verses.m: That which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from the clarity of one's own understanding, is called sattvic happiness.
verses.sa: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥

verses.m: The happiness that comes from contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is called rajasic.
verses.sa: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥

chains.summary: Pleasures born of contact are wombs of sorrow. They begin and end. The wise do not delight in them. Unhooked from outer contacts one finds the joy that is in the self. Whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here is happy.
chains.title: Pleasures with a beginning and an end

verses.m: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
verses.sa: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥

verses.m: The enjoyments born of contact are wombs of sorrow; they have a beginning and an end, Kaunteya. The wise do not delight in them.
verses.sa: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥

verses.m: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
verses.sa: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥

chains.summary: Each higher joy is a hundred times the one below. Each equals the joy of the learned person who is not struck by desire. Knowing that joy, one fears nothing. One is no longer tormented by wondering why one did not do right and why one did wrong.
chains.title: The measure of joy

verses.m: Now an inquiry into joy. Let there be a young man, good, well read, quick, firm and strong, and let this whole earth full of wealth be his: that is one measure of human joy. A hundred human joys make one joy of the human gandharvas, and so too is the joy of a learned one untouched by desire.
verses.sa: सैषाऽऽनन्दस्य मीमाꣳसा भवति । युवा स्यात्साधुयुवाऽध्यायकः । आशिष्ठो दृढिष्ठो बलिष्ठः । तस्येयं पृथिवी सर्वा वित्तस्य पूर्णा स्यात् । स एको मानुष आनन्दः । ते ये शतं मानुषा आनन्दाः । स एको मनुष्यगन्धर्वाणामानन्दः । श्रोत्रियस्य चाकामहतस्य ।

verses.m: That from which words turn back, along with the mind, not reaching it: whoever knows the joy of Brahman fears nothing at all.
verses.sa: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्। न बिभेति कुतश्चनेति ।

verses.m: Such a one is no longer tormented by the thought: why did I not do good? Why did I do wrong?
verses.sa: एतꣳह वाव न तपति । किमहꣳसाधु नाकरवम् । किमहं पापमकरवमिति ।

depicts.m: With minds fixed on me and lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and delighted.
depicts.sa: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
depicts.why: Devotees pictured delighting together in talk of him.

gloss: Joy that does not depend on getting. The Taittiriya says from joy beings are born. The Chandogya says happiness is in the vast, not the small.

hero.m: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
hero.sa: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥

loci.m: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
loci.sa: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥

loci.m: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The infinite alone is happiness. So the infinite must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand the infinite.'
loci.sa: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥

loci.m: That which is well made is the essence itself. Having found that essence, a person becomes joyful.
loci.sa: यद्वै तत् सुकृतम् रसो वै सः रसꣳह्येवायं लब्ध्वाऽऽनन्दी भवति ।

practices.m: Do not stir your mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. Be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self.
practices.sa: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
practices.why: Shows the self is called ananda-vigraha.

practices.m: Even a particular form is not recognised without its name, though it sit in the palm of your hand. But remember the name without seeing the form, and a special love rises in the heart.
practices.sa: रूप बिसेष नाम बिनु जानें। करतल गत न परहिं पहिचानें॥ सुमिरिअ नाम रूप बिनु देखें। आवत हृदयँ सनेह बिसेषें ॥
practices.why: Cultivates love that rises with the name.

practices.m: He sits happily, sleeps happily, comes and goes happily, speaks and eats happily: calm-minded even in daily affairs.
practices.sa: सुखमास्ते सुखं शेते सुखमायाति याति च । सुखं वक्ति सुखं भुङ्क्ते व्यवहारेऽपि शान्तधीः ॥

practices.m: I have found the jewel-wealth of Ram's name. My true teacher gave me a priceless thing and in kindness made me his own. I found the savings of many lives and lost all the world's. Spending does not exhaust it, no thief can steal it; it grows day by day.
practices.sa: पायो जी म्हें तो राम रतन धन पायो। वस्तु अमोलक दी म्हारे सतगुरू, किरपा कर अपनायो॥ जनम-जनम की पूँजी पाई, जग में सभी खोवायो। खरच न खूटै चोर न लूटै, दिन-दिन बढ़त सवायो॥
practices.why: Shows the joy of having found.

practices.m: The all-pervading, stainless, formless Absolute, beyond all play, the unborn one, lies in Kausalya's lap, won over by love and devotion.
practices.sa: ब्यापक ब्रह्म निरंजन निर्गुन बिगत बिनोद। सो अज प्रेम भगति बस कौसल्या कें गोद ॥
practices.why: Holds the infinite as a child.

practices.m: Friend, put all the joys of heaven and liberation on one side of the scale: together they cannot match the joy of a single moment of good company.
practices.sa: तात स्वर्ग अपबर्ग सुख धरिअ तुला एक अंग। तूल न ताहि सकल मिलि जो सुख लव सतसंग ॥
practices.why: Shows the joy of being with the good.

practices.m: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The infinite alone is happiness. So the infinite must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand the infinite.'
practices.sa: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
practices.why: Points happiness to what has no edge.

practices.m: He understood that joy is Brahman. From joy these beings are born, by joy they live once born, and into joy they enter at death. This is the wisdom of Bhrigu and Varuna, established in the highest space. Whoever knows this becomes established.
practices.sa: आनन्दो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात्। आनन्दाध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । आनन्देन जातानि जीवन्ति । आनन्दं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । सैषा भार्गवी वारुणी विद्या । परमे व्योमन्प्रतिष्ठिता ।स य एवं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति ।
practices.why: Names joy as the source one comes from and lives by.

stories.l: Forgiveness can mean going first to the person who hurt you and putting them at ease.
stories.s: Bharat walks barefoot to Chitrakoot and falls at Ram's feet; Ram lifts him into his arms. Ram learns his father has died and grieves. When the queens arrive, Ram goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused it all, falls at her feet and comforts her, blaming no one.

stories.l: Some exchanges can't be priced; gratitude can be payment enough.
stories.s: At the Ganga, a boatman refuses to take Ram across until he can wash his feet, joking that if the dust of those feet turned a stone into a woman, it might turn his boat, his family's livelihood, into one too. Ram laughs and agrees. On the far bank Sita offers her ring as fare, and Kevat refuses: after a lifetime of wages, today he has been paid in full.

stories.l: A lost role can be met with grace; sometimes it even feels like freedom.
stories.s: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.
stories.t: Ram hears he is to be exiled

stories.l: Even in a hostile place there may be one ally; find them.
stories.s: Searching Lanka, Hanuman is surprised to find a house with Ram's name on it. Its owner, Vibhishan, Ravana's brother, says he lives in Lanka like a tongue among teeth. Hanuman tells him even a restless monkey like himself was given Ram's love.
stories.t: Hanuman finds a friend in Lanka
